The move concludes a major southern separatist chapter, pivoting talks toward federalism. description:
Fishing remains the backbone of Greenland’s economy and a way of life for many communities.
However, US President Donald Trump is focused on the island’s vast, largely untapped mineral wealth, amid competition with China over rare earth supplies.
Greenland holds deposits of rare earths and metals vital for technology and military industries currently dominated by China.
Local fishermen say they value freedom, tradition and ties to Denmark over US control.
Harsh conditions and limited infrastructure mean most resources remain unexploited.
Some Greenlanders see minerals as a path to future independence, but not as a pawn in a US–China rivalry.

Al Jazeera’s Rory Challands reports from Ilulissat in western Greenland.

description:
Sudan’s government has officially returned to the capital, Khartoum, for the first time since the war started in 2023.
The government had been operating from the Red Sea city of Port Sudan.
It's been eight months since the Sudanese army announced it had regained full control of Khartoum from the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.
The conflict has led to what the United Nations describes as the world’s worst humanitarian crisis.

The governor of Darfur says a joint military operation is being carried out in Darfur and North Kordofan to liberate the regions from the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
Sudan's army says the preparations ahead of a possible full-scale launch have already forced the RSF to retreat from border areas.
The governor of Darfur says the operation has so far prevented the paramilitary RSF from laying siege on el-Obeid in North Kordofan.

Al Jazeera’s Hiba Morgan has more from Khartoum, Sudan.

Among the issues, at least 3.5 million people have been displaced by the ongoing civil war.
They won’t be able to vote. 

Al Jazeera’s Tony Cheng visited a community where people have been displaced by war and where the election appears to mean very little.

description:
US President Donald Trump says his country will acquire the Danish territory of Greenland.
That's despite Denmark saying the island is not for sale and Greenlanders saying they have no desire to become part of the United States. 
Trump has been pushing for the island to come under US ownership. 
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will meet with Denmark's Foreign Minister next week to discuss the issue.
Trump had suggested buying the island from Denmark and at one point threatened military action. 

Several European leaders have condemned the idea of a US-takeover of Greenland.
Germany's vice chancellor is among those who have urged Washington to respect Greenland’s sovereignty.

Al Jazeera's Rory Challands reports from Ilulissat in western Greenland.

US prosecutors have opened a criminal probe into Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell.
The Department of Justice says it's investigating ⁠statements Powell made to Congress, and whether he lied on the scope of renovating Federal Reserve buildings.
The Fed chair has called the new threat “a pretext” to pile pressure, in a dispute with the Trump Administration over lowering interest rates.

Eric Ham is a political analyst and the author of the book “The GOP Civil War: Inside the Battle for the Soul of the Republican Party”.
He says interference in monetary policy is affecting trust in the US standing around the world.

Iran's president Masoud Pezeshkian has accused what he calls “rioters” and “terrorist elements” of hijacking antigovernment demonstrations and causing havoc. 
Masoud Pezeshkian addressed the unrest in a television interview as the protests enter a third week.
President Donald Trump has said the US will “hit Iran where it hurts” if protesters are killed. 
Tehran hasn't confirmed the number of demonstrators who have died. 
Three days of mourning have been declared in the country.

Al Jazeera’s Hamza Mohamed reports.
